tasks.short: Watch the patient and monitors during anaesthesia, tell the anaesthesiologist about changes and record events.

steps.what: Nurse watches the monitor: heart rate, blood pressure, saturation, ventilation, depth
Nurse observes the patient and surgical field for colour, position and blood loss
Nurse informs the physician of the patient's condition during anesthesia
Anaesthesiologist decides and orders the action to take

Nurse records events, drugs given and fluids in the anaesthesia record: typed today; after the change drug and concentration come from the scanned syringe or bag label and the nurse enters the dose and events

tasks.design: Configure the anaesthesia record ({OTHER}) with quick-event buttons and barcode scanning of labelled syringes and fluid bags, so drug names and concentrations come from the label while vital signs keep charting from the monitor; the nurse still enters doses given and events, which are first records. Watching, judging and telling the anaesthesiologist do not change.
tasks.previous_blocker: Events and drugs were typed or handwritten in the middle of the case.
tasks.enabler_now: Anaesthesia record systems support barcode scanning and event buttons as configuration.
tasks.still_hard: Vigilance during anaesthesia is the job; no tool takes over noticing and speaking up.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing a change before the alarm sounds and telling the anaesthesiologist clearly and early.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; less typing during the case.

reach.task: Record drugs and events during anaesthesia
reach.learn: Whether barcode scanning cuts recording errors in the record.

evidence.claim: Anaesthesia record systems can take drug entries by barcode scan and events by quick buttons.
The medical record is kept twenty years after the last change.
The inspectorate names medication errors from wrong registration as a risk providers must manage.

assumptions: Boundary: from induction to the end of the case in theatre; recovery is outside.
Input contract: syringe and fluid labels with barcodes, produced by the pharmacy or the labelling printer in theatre; vital signs from the monitor; fallback is typing.
Vital signs already chart automatically; that runtime earns no saving.
Anaesthesiologist time is outside the nurse's savings.
s5 keeps 65: the label fills drug and concentration, but the dose actually given and each event are the nurse's own record; quick-event buttons instead of typing are not counted as a saving.
unknowns: Whether syringes are labelled with barcodes in theatre.
How the anaesthesia record is kept today.
research_questions: Do scanned entries reduce missing or wrong drug records?

incremental.description: Nurse fixes scans that fail and enters unlabelled drugs by hand.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: theatres without barcode labels keep entering drugs by hand, so s5 keeps 100 (-0.5); high: labelled syringes and bags in every theatre (5.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take part in nursing research: frame a question, search and read literature, collect and analyse data, report.

steps.what: Nurse formulates a practice question with the nurse researcher
Nurse searches literature databases and guidelines for research related to nursing
Nurse screens articles, reads them and summarises the evidence

loop.input: Titles and abstracts from the search, and the inclusion criteria set by the nurse and researcher.
loop.output: Include or exclude per article with the reason, plus an evidence table row for included articles.
loop.check: Every include must quote the abstract sentence that meets each criterion, and the nurse reads each quote to see it really meets the criterion; a random 20% is screened blind by the nurse; if agreement falls below the set level, the nurse screens all; the nurse reads every included article in full before it enters the evidence table.
loop.stop: One pass per article; unclear ones go to the nurse.
loop.why_not_simpler: Abstracts describe populations and outcomes in varied words; keyword filters miss or over-include.

steps.what: Privacy officer reviews and approves the request for patient record data
Nurse collects audit data from patient records into a spreadsheet
Nurse analyses the data with the nurse researcher
Nurse researcher guides the method and checks the analysis
Nurse writes up findings and presents them to the ward or a conference

tasks.design: Saved searches with alerts run in the literature databases; a bounded model step screens abstracts against the inclusion criteria and fills an evidence table, each include quoting the matching sentence, with a blind sample screened by the nurse. Once the privacy officer approves the data request, a governed query on the {DATA_PLATFORM} extracts the audit fields from the record instead of hand copying, and a report template in {DOCS} takes the evidence table and results.
tasks.previous_blocker: Screening and chart review were done by hand in spare hours, so ward nurses rarely took part in research.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models screen abstracts when quotes and sampling check them, and governed data platforms can extract record fields under approval.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing the question and judging evidence quality need training; record data needs privacy approval and often cleaning.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which practice problem is worth studying and turning findings into changes on the ward.

ambition.what: Ward nurses without research time who can join a project because screening and data collection take days, not months.

tasks.altitude: The nurse frames, checks and interprets rather than screens and copies; method decisions stay with the researcher.

reach.task: Update nursing protocols from new evidence
reach.learn: Whether the screened evidence tables can feed protocol reviews.

evidence.claim: Literature work can use an artefact generator with citations, approved by a committee.
Health data is special category; research use of record data needs a legal basis, privacy review and usually a DPIA, with national rules on research without consent.
Providers are responsible for careful use of generative AI, including testing and monitoring.

assumptions: Boundary: from the practice question to findings presented; implementing changes is outside.

Input contract: inclusion criteria set by the nurse and researcher; record fields for the audit defined in the data request and extracted by the clinical data team's query; fallback is hand screening and chart review.
Scenario: a small audit-type study, not a trial needing ethics committee review.
Privacy officer and researcher time is outside the nurse's savings.

s2 keeps 80 for reading alerts and running new searches. s3 keeps 50 for the blind sample, reading quotes and reading included articles. s5 keeps 40 for checking the extracted data against a sample of records. s8 keeps 85 because the findings are written by the nurse; the template fills tables and layout.
unknowns: Whether the hospital has a governed data platform with record extracts.
How often ward nurses join research projects.
research_questions: How does screening agreement between the model step and nurses vary by topic?

already_counted.description: Nurse blind-screens the 20% sample and checks the evidence table.
Nurse checks extracted data against a sample of records.

incremental.description: Nurse writes precise inclusion criteria and data definitions for each study.
Clinical data team builds and maintains extraction queries.

approvals.approved_version: Data request with fields, period and patient group as approved by the privacy officer in s4; any extra field needs a new approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: abstracts on the topic fail the agreement check, so the nurse screens nearly all (s3 keeps 90), and the study needs new data collection, so s5 keeps 100 (6.6); high: screening passes and the audit fields come from the query (28.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The nurse keeps vigilance in theatre and judgement in research; typing and hand screening shrink.
skills_to_grow: Writing inclusion criteria and data definitions
Checking screened evidence and extracted data
role.ambitious_version: A ward nurse who runs a small evidence project each year because screening and data collection no longer eat spare evenings.
